body.en: Analyze one-variable distributions: center (mean, median), spread (standard deviation, range), frequency tables and histograms, and survey margins of error.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error)

body.en:
Why Shifting Data Preserves Standard Deviation while Scaling Multiplies It: Suppose a dataset \(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n\) has mean \(\bar{x}\) and standard deviation \(s_x = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n-1}\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}\). If every value is transformed linearly via \(y_i = ax_i + b\), the new mean is \(\bar{y} = a\bar{x} + b\). Each deviation from the new mean becomes:

\[ y_i - \bar{y} = (ax_i + b) - (a\bar{x} + b) = a(x_i - \bar{x}) \]

Notice that the additive shift \(+b\) cancels out completely! Consequently, adding or subtracting a constant \(b\) to every data value leaves the standard deviation and range unchanged, whereas multiplying every value by \(a\) scales both the range and standard deviation by \(|a|\).

Eight salaries (thousands): 30, 32, 35, 36, 37, 38, 40, 120.

Mean \(= 368/8 = 46\). Median \(= (36+37)/2 = 36.5\).

The outlier ($120k) inflates the mean. The median better represents the typical salary.

Assuming a larger range always guarantees a larger standard deviation
Range only depends on the two extreme endpoints, while standard deviation depends on how all points cluster around the mean.
Compare how tightly the bulk of the data points cluster near the mean versus the tails.

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error

body.en: Exam Strategy (College Board Digital SAT Math): You never need to compute standard deviation by hand on the Digital SAT. Instead, compare distributions visually: whichever dot plot or histogram has more data points pushed far away from the center (and fewer stacked at the mean) has the larger standard deviation.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

A list of 8 test scores is: 68, 72, 75, 78, 82, 85, 90, 94. What is the positive difference between the range and the median of this dataset?
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

A list of 8 test scores is: 68, 72, 75, 78, 82, 85, 90, 94. What is the positive dإذا كانference between the range and the median of this dataset?

solution.en:
Step 1: Find the median of the 8 sorted scores (average of the 4th and 5th values): \( (78 + 82)/2 = 80 \).

Step 2: Find the range (maximum minus minimum): \( 94 - 68 = 26 \).

Step 3: Compute the positive difference between the median and the range: \( 80 - 26 = 54 \).

label.en: ⚠️ SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Statistics, Sampling & Margin of Error

body.en:
• Margin of Error Depends on Sample Size, NOT Population: Increasing the sample size (\( n \)) reduces the margin of error (proportional to \( 1/\sqrt{n} \)). The total population size has negligible impact on margin of error.
  • Generalization Boundaries: A random sample can only be generalized to the population from which the sample was drawn. A survey of visitors at an athletic store cannot generalize to all city residents.
  • Outlier Pull: Extreme high outliers pull the mean upward without significantly shifting the median ( \text{Mean} > \text{Median} for right-skewed data). For skewed data with extreme outliers, the median is a more resistant measure of center than the mean.
  • Standard Deviation Definition: Standard deviation measures the spread or dispersion of values around the mean. Two datasets can have the same mean and range but very different standard deviations if values are clustered tightly vs. spread toward extremes.

Set A: {10, 10, 10, 10}.  Set B: {4, 8, 12, 16}. Both have mean 10.

Set A has \( \text{SD} = 0 \) (all values equal the mean). Set B has a substantially larger standard deviation because its values are dispersed farther from 10.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Two data sets have the same mean of 50 and the same sample size of 100. Dataset A has a standard deviation of 3.2, and Dataset B has a standard deviation of 8.9. Which statement must be true?

(A) Dataset A values are more spread out from the mean than Dataset B values.
(B) Dataset B has greater variability about the mean than Dataset A.
(C) Both datasets have identical minimum and maximum values.
(D) Dataset B has more outliers than Dataset A.
question.ar:
حل المسألة التالية في (One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error): Level 2 · Medium

Two data sets have the same mean of 50 and the same sample size of 100. Dataset A has a standard deviation of 3.2, and Dataset B has a standard deviation of 8.9. Which statement must be true?

(A) Dataset A values are more spread out from the mean than Dataset B values.
(B) Dataset B has greater variability about the mean than Dataset A.
(C) Both datasets have identical minimum and maximum values.
(D) Dataset B has more outliers than Dataset A.

solution.en:
Correct Answer: (B).

Standard deviation measures the typical distance of data values from their mean. A larger standard deviation directly corresponds to greater variability or dispersion about the mean.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Margin of Error & Generalization Boundaries

body.en: Calculate confidence intervals from survey estimates, understand how sample size \( n \) scales margin of error (\( 1/\sqrt{n} \)), and restrict conclusions to sampled populations.

Problem: A poll of 600 randomly selected registered voters finds that 54% support a proposition, with an associated margin of error of \( \pm 3\% \). Can we conclude that a majority of all voters nationwide support the proposition?

Solution: The confidence interval is \( 54\% \pm 3\% = [51\%, 57\%] \). While every value in the interval exceeds 50% (indicating a probable majority), the conclusion generalizes only to the specific population of registered voters sampled, not to all voters nationwide unless the sample was drawn from that exact national population.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

A school administrator randomly surveys 120 high school seniors at Oakwood High School. In the sample, 65% report planning to attend a four-year college, with a margin of error of \( \pm 4\% \). Which of the following conclusions is most statistically sound?

(A) Exactly 65% of all Oakwood High seniors will attend college.
(B) It is plausible that between 61% and 69% of all Oakwood High seniors plan to attend a four-year college.
(C) Between 61% and 69% of all high school seniors in the state plan to attend college.
(D) To reduce the margin of error by half, the administrator should survey 240 seniors.
question.ar:
حل المسألة التالية في (One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error): Level 3 · Advanced

A school administrator randomly surveys 120 high school seniors at Oakwood High School. In the sample, 65% report planning to attend a four-year college, with a margin of error of \( \pm 4\% \). Which of the following conclusions is most statistically sound?

(A) Exactly 65% of all Oakwood High seniors will attend college.
(B) It is plausible that between 61% and 69% of all Oakwood High seniors plan to attend a four-year college.
(C) Between 61% and 69% of all high school seniors in the state plan to attend college.
(D) To reduce the margin of error by half, the administrator should survey 240 seniors.

solution.en:
Correct Answer: (B).

The margin of error creates a plausible confidence interval \( 65\% \pm 4\% = [61\%, 69\%] \). Because the random sample was drawn exclusively from Oakwood High seniors, the conclusion generalizes only to that school's senior class (eliminating C). To halve the margin of error, sample size must quadruple (\( 4 \times 120 = 480 \)), making D incorrect.

label.en: Level 4 (Synthesis) — Effect of Linear Data Scaling on Standard Deviation

body.en:
Problem: Data set \( X \) has a mean of 40 and a standard deviation of 6. Data set \( Y \) is formed by multiplying every value in \( X \) by 3 and subtracting 10 (\( Y = 3X - 10 \)). What are the mean and standard deviation of \( Y \)?

Solution: Mean shifts and scales: \( \mu_Y = 3(40) - 10 = 110 \). Standard deviation measures spread, so adding/subtracting 10 has zero effect on it; only multiplying by \( |3| \) scales it: \( \sigma_Y = 3 \times 6 = 18 \).

question.en:
Level 4 · Synthesis

A random sample of 400 registered voters in a city of 50,000 voters found that 55% support a transit bond, with an associated margin of error of 4.8% at the 95% confidence level. If a second survey uses a random sample of 1,600 registered voters from the same city, what will be the new margin of error?
question.ar:
Level 4 · Synthesis

A random sample of 400 registered voters in a city of 50,000 voters found that 55% support a transit bond, with an associated margin of error of 4.8% at the 95% confidence level. إذا كان a second survey uses a random sample of 1,600 registered voters from the same city, what will be the new margin of error?

solution.en:
Margin of error is inversely proportional to \( \sqrt{n} \). Multiplying the sample size by 4 (from 400 to 1,600) divides the margin of error by \( \sqrt{4} = 2 \):

\[ \text{New Margin of Error} = \frac{4.8\%}{2} = 2.4\%. \]
